name: INFRA-ART Spectral Library: Raman reference spectra of art-related materials (Cortea et al. 2023, INOE 2000; frozen 2026-10-21 snapshot)
description: Raman reference spectra of 186 art-related materials from the INFRA-ART Spectral Library (Cortea et al. 2023, doi:10.1145/3593427; FAIRsharing doi:10.25504/FAIRsharing.091c24), operated by the National Institute for Research and Development in Optoelectronics (INOE 2000, Bucharest, Romania). Frozen 2026-10-21 snapshot: at capture time the library held 1,209 reference samples (3,161 spectra across FTIR, XRF, Raman and SWIR), of which 186 carry a Raman spectrum (one per sample). Each spectrum is the original Renishaw ENLIGHTEN CSV export as served by the site (WP 785 ER spectrometer, 785.078 nm excitation; per-measurement parameters - integration time 0.1-10 s, scan averaging, ROI - are recorded in the CSV metadata block), acquired 2022-03-30 to 2025-06-06. Task: material-class classification - labels are the library's 12 material classes (Special effect pigments 61, Earth pigments 43, Resins, balsams and wax 23, Glues, gums and binders 19, Inorganic pigments, synthetic 18, Organic dyes and pigments, synthetic 5, Mineral pigments 4, Carbon-based pigments 4, Mixed pigments 3, Unclassified materials 3, Natural organic dyes and pigments 2, Other mixtures 1); the per-sample material names, formulas and sources are in the snapshot manifest (5 names are shared by two different samples). Native 1666-point axis 160.07-3,215.39 cm^-1 (non-uniform spacing, identical in all files), used as is - no resampling. Intensities are the Processed (dark-subtracted) column in arbitrary units; the integration time varies per sample (0.1-10 s), so absolute intensity scales are not comparable across spectra and models should rely on relative peak structure (a few points go slightly negative, minimum -13). Two CSV header variants occur (7 columns including Raw/Dark/Reference, 122 files; 4 columns, 64 files); the loader parses header-driven. Served from a frozen zip snapshot (186 CSVs + manifest.json + README.txt, size + sha256 pinned) mirrored at HTW-KI-Werkstatt/RamanBench (infra_art/): the live endpoint (https://infra-art.eu/api/samples/spectra-file?sampleId=<id>&dataType=Raman%20Spectrum) requires full browser request headers (the site is behind Cloudflare) and the library is still growing, so the snapshot is the reproducible reference. is_grouped=False (one spectrum per physical sample, no replicate structure). License: CC BY-NC 4.0 (as stated on the site; non-commercial use only).

rai:dataCollection: Raman measurements of 186 art-related reference materials (pigments, resins/balsams/wax, glues/gums/binders, dyes and effect materials) acquired 2022-03-30 to 2025-06-06 at INOE 2000, Bucharest; Renishaw WP 785 ER, 785.078 nm excitation, per-measurement parameters (integration time, scan averaging, ROI) recorded in each file.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Dark subtraction is applied by the instrument (Processed = Raw - Dark columns); the export records 'Raman Intensity Corrected: FALSE' and no baseline correction. The loader applies no baseline correction, normalization or resampling; the native 1666-point axis is used as is. Both ENLIGHTEN CSV header variants (7 columns including Raw/Dark/Reference in 122 files; 4 columns in 64) are parsed header-driven.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each sample is a reference material with a documented identity: name, alternative names, chemical formula, source and material class (12 classes) are recorded in the library; the class assignments were made by the library's curators (INOE 2000) as part of building the library, not for this benchmark. No human labelling of the spectra themselves was involved. Five material names are shared by two different samples (different sources/lots); sample-level identifiers are preserved in the snapshot manifest.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No personal or sensitive information is included. All samples are inorganic and organic art materials (pigments, resins, glues, binders, dyes) without any human identifiers.
rai:dataBiases: Single instrument (Renishaw WP 785 ER, 785 nm), single lab and one measurement-protocol family, so results may not transfer to other instruments or excitation wavelengths. Class balance is skewed (61-1 spectra per class; smallest class 'Other mixtures' has a single spectrum). Per-sample integration time varies from 0.1 to 10 s, so absolute intensity scales are not comparable across spectra (the transferable signal is relative peak structure). 'Mixed pigments' (3), 'Other mixtures' (1) and 'Unclassified materials' (3) are coarse or undefined categories. The snapshot reflects the library as of 2026-10-21 (186 of 1,209 samples carried a Raman spectrum at that time).
rai:dataLimitations: Single instrument/lab and protocol family; skewed class balance (61...1 spectra per class); three coarse or undefined material classes (Mixed pigments 3, Unclassified materials 3, Other mixtures 1); one spectrum per physical sample (no replicates, so no group-aware splitting); absolute intensities not comparable across samples (integration time 0.1-10 s); non-uniform wavenumber axis (~2.2-2.6 cm^-1 steps); a few intensity points are slightly negative (dark subtraction); frozen 2026-10-21 snapshot of a still-growing library; the CC BY-NC 4.0 license restricts commercial use.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Supports heritage science: identification of art-related materials (pigments, binders, resins) for conservation, authentication and education; no human or medical use. Results are tied to a single 785 nm instrument, and any identification of real heritage samples requires validation against independent measurements.
rai:dataUseCases: Material-class classification from a single Raman spectrum (12 classes); the library also serves as a spectral matching reference for unknown heritage materials (per-sample names/formulas in the manifest); note the single-spectrum-per-class tail (1-5 spectra) and the coarse classes when evaluating models.
